summaries.demographer: Kennedi Terry is a 40-year-old Black/African-American woman living alone in an owned townhouse in Glassboro, New Jersey, with no spouse, partner, or children (Q51, Q58, Q84, Q89). She was born in Camden, raised in South Jersey, lived with both parents and an older brother at age 16, and remains closely tied to parents, sibling, niece, nephew, church, and community networks (Q05, Q87, Q97-Q99). She has a bachelor's degree in information systems from Rowan University and works full time as a senior network and systems administrator, placing her in a stable middle-class professional position (Q65, Q72, Q90). Her household income is from her own salaried employment, with homeownership, retirement savings, and remaining student, car, and mortgage debt shaping her life-course position (Q61-Q63, Q74).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Kennedi is a disciplined planner who uses routines, automatic savings, spreadsheets, documentation, and preventive maintenance to reduce uncertainty (Q15, Q61, Q65). She is risk-aware rather than risk-avoidant: she chose the harder technical career path, bought a home, and occasionally splurges on camera gear or jazz, but she keeps emergency savings and avoids reckless credit use (Q02, Q56, Q58, Q82). Her choices are identity-linked, especially around family responsibility, Black community mentorship, professional competence, and self-sufficiency (Q17, Q28, Q83, Q108). She shows long time horizons through certification planning, retirement saving, health management, and a dream Ghana trip funded gradually rather than impulsively (Q18, Q31, Q62, Q108).
summaries.political_scientist: Kennedi is a regular voter and fairly strong Democrat with practical progressive views on civil rights, healthcare, education, labor fairness, voting rights, racial equity, and institutional competence (Q23-Q24, Q95-Q96). She has become more attentive to local governance, school boards, misinformation, and implementation after the pandemic and recent political conflicts (Q25). Black Lives Matter and policing issues affected her deeply, leading to family conversations, a vigil, a peaceful march, workplace equity discussions, and stronger views on accountability and prevention (Q26-Q30). Her civic orientation is participatory but pragmatic, combining voting, community tutoring, church/community ties, and mentorship rather than constant public protest (Q17, Q23, Q29).
summaries.psychologist: Kennedi presents as conscientious, routine-oriented, technically analytical, and community-minded, with a self-concept built around reliability, competence, and making room for others (Q01, Q15, Q65, Q109). She also has a spontaneous and creative side expressed through photography, live music, travel dreams, cooking, and occasional camera or jazz-ticket splurges (Q48, Q56, Q108). Emotionally, she reports no clinical depression but does experience work-linked anxiety symptoms, especially around cybersecurity incidents, responsibility, and sleep disruption (Q43-Q45). Her coping style combines problem-solving, documentation, walking, prayer, music, journaling, close friendships, and selective counseling, showing both self-reliance and willingness to seek support when stress exceeds routine coping (Q38, Q44-Q47).
